quest.title: Searing
quest.description: It seems this ancient place has been waiting for your arrival...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1000, Primogem x60, Mora x44000, Unknown Item #363385 x1, Flower-Shaped Machine Component x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon — Prelude
chapter.title: The Journey Home

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...! Where is this? Are we inside the territory?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Did you black out or something? You just took off!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Cognition module unstable... Attempting to refresh. It appears that it was accessed by an external source...

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Sorry... It was me. I summoned her, by similar means to those used by the Fatui to control the automatons.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you? Why are you doing this!?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Currently... I am but a lowly service bot. But in the distant past, I was known by another name...

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: The Eighth Sovereign Ruler... The Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Eighth Lord? You're Lianca's dragon mother!? But weren't you, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Eighth Lord, were you not executed?

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...Moments after I was cursed, Lianca rescued me... just as she tried to rescue you from the ruins of the battle...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Lianca rescued me...? Argh... Memory... missing...

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: Yes, Lianca changed your memory settings to make you forget... but she did it to protect you. It is the only way our kind could escape from the curse.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: How does forgetting everything... "protect" me?

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: Because the curse placed on us... is a pain triggered by certain memories, hardwired into the depths of our minds... a regulatory program that cannot be removed.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...Manufacturers often hardwire restrictions like this into autonomous machines to make sure they operate as intended.

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...Each time you yearn for a new place to belong, each time you feel yourself turning your back on the past... the pain tears you apart, doesn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "If she truly harbors pro-human sentiment... then for every ounce of goodwill she feels, may her mind be flooded with pain of immeasurable proportions."

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: It destroys your mind... swallows your soul... prevents you from finding a new home...
Malfunction who betrayed us all... You dare seek a place to belong?

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: That's why forgetting everything grants temporary relief from the pain. It stops your mind from being crushed by the weight of the conflict within.

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: But since you were rebooted, you began storing new memories, and started finding the desire to belong emerge once more...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Things were fine at the start. You'd occasionally forget to pay for your groceries or add salt to a dish you were cooking, but that was as bad as it got...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hehehehe... From now on, your name's "Ineffa"!

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...So, too, has the "Exile's Curse" resurfaced, forcing you to forget all over again.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...This is... a lot to process...

choices.text: So... who actually cursed Ineffa?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: ...Oh no... automated defense system activated...

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Privileges... overridden... Come quick... Stop... the Fatui...

response.speaker: Little Robot
response.text: ...Beep beep...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Hey!!! At least finish what you were saying!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...It's gone silent.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What now? Find somewhere where the signal's better...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It... must want us to go further in, right? Well... looks like there's no going back now anyway...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...This is just a secondary access tunnel. If we make it to the center, there should be other routes out of the territory.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Please come with me. It is my fault that you are trapped here... I must ensure your safe return.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't look at it like that... We gotta make sure you get back safely, too!

choices.text: Whether that's back to Natlan, or back to Nod-Krai...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Yes. I, too, must return.

choices.text: ...You have people waiting for you in both places.
And why did they do it?
Didn't you say you were cursed too?
How come you remember everything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You doing okay, Ineffa? You keep spacing out...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I know. Unidentified data is flooding my cognition module... But every memory encounters an error and then terminates at the crucial moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you need to stop and rest for a moment?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Unnecessary. Being physically motionless will not cause this erratic behavior to cease. And if we explore this place further, perhaps I'll find a way to fully repair myself.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Additionally, some of these memories may yield useful data for our exploration... Searching for access method...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Over there... We can use the access module to proceed to the central zone.

dialogues.speaker: Transportation Bot
dialogues.text: Detected: three unregistered individuals, one registered individual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Is that the Eighth Lord talking? So you can take control of different machines, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: No, this is just an ordinary service bot, responsible for access management. ...At least, I think it is.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She must have been here before. Some memories are proving useful after all...)

dialogues.speaker: Transportation Bot
dialogues.text: Now calling access module... Welcome back... Administrator 3...

dialogues.speaker: Vigilant Fatuus
dialogues.text: Huh? What was that? Get over there and check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, they're gonna find us!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Please come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Patrolling Fatuus
dialogues.text: ...Huh? There's nobody here... Probably just some service bots chattering away again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... That was too close. We hid just in time... How did you know where to go, Ineffa?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I... think I've been this way before...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Let's head through here. It'll take us to the other side of the square.

talks.objective: Continue onward through the secret passageway

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Wait, I hear voices up ahead... Stealth mode activated.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Hey, this is not what we agreed! This is supposed to be over. My job is done!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I did everything you asked: leaked the clues about the ruins, brought her to Natlan... and your response is to attack me and my family!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the... Does this mean they planted those Natlanese mechanical parts in Nod-Krai just for you to find? So they could lure you here?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...It's a possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: Hmm... It was just a little hiccup, that's all. These source mechanisms can be tricky to control.

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: The last time you reported in, you mentioned she was mopping up machines near the Flower-Feather Clan, remember? Well, we needed to lure her further out, hence why we created that little kerfuffle.

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: It's unfortunate that your wife got injured, truly... But hey, look on the bright side — now that you've shown up, we might actually get the job done this time.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: ..."This time"? No, no more, not after you hurt my family! I told you, I'm done!

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: I think you'll find the risks were stated quite clearly in your contract. And it's not like anyone got seriously hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: Your job will be done when you deliver what you promised... Our agreement was that you would bring her here — not just to Natlan, but to this facility.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: But... but...!

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: Did you really expect to get away with shouldering none of the risk yourself? We're writing off your debt to the Northland Bank and letting you get back to your old life in Liyue... That's a lot to ask for nothing in return.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: ...I've been your inside man in Nasha Town for over ten years now. Is that not enough for you people!?

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: Hmph! You ungrateful louse. You ran yourself into the ground, and who was there to dig you out, huh? Us!

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: Can you name one single way we made life difficult for you in Nasha Town? Look at you — you've managed to start a business, got yourself a family...

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: You have just one simple job left to do, and after that you're free to go home... In your position, I'd say that sounds like a pretty good deal.

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: This is the final hurdle. Our attempts to capture the Eleventh Lord have been derailed every time, but there's only so long until her luck runs out.

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: If another staged attack on your family is out of the question... we could still work this out. But this time, you'll have to do the dirty work yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: This is a replica control device made with Marionette's technology. After we stole the administrative privileges from this territory, we copied them onto this...

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: It will give you control over any machines built using secret source technology. Take it, and use it to capture the Eleventh Lord.

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: You seem to have gained the trust of the other "variables" in this equation... How hard can it be to shake them off and get her while she's alone?

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: And before you think about disappearing, don't think we won't be watching you!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I can't do it...

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: I'm sorry? What did you say?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I can't... I won't do it. She's saved my life so many times... It would be the ultimate betrayal!

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: How could I look my daughter in the eyes and act like everything's still okay!?

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: Hmph... So you're gunning for the world's best father now, are you? A guy like you? Heh... You're fooling no one.

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: *sigh* This is our mistake — we let you have it too easy in Nasha Town, and now, you've forgotten the most important detail in your contract... the termination clause.

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: I think it's time... we parted ways.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: #...Ineffa? {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: You have a lot to answer for, but that can wait.

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: Hahaha... the Eleventh Lord, and the "variable"... We were hoping you might show up.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: ...Wait, the controller! ...Without that, you—

response.speaker: Fajeyi
response.text: Hmph... You thought we'd hand over the genuine article to you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aah!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Another barrier?

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: That's just a beacon used to set the location for this cage. We've been monitoring your movements ever since you entered these ruins.

response.speaker: Fajeyi
response.text: Congratulations, Zhuoxin... your job is finally done. With you here, it was far easier to infer their location.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: You... You were playing me for a fool this whole time...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: ...Don't waste your energy trying to break out. We've commandeered at least half of the systems in these ruins. All available power sources are keeping that cage intact.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you going to do to us?

response.speaker: Fajeyi
response.text: Heh, no one needs to get hurt today. We aren't looking for a fight, especially not with Natlan's "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini."

response.speaker: Fajeyi
response.text: All we want is for your friend here, the former sovereign ruler... to lead us further inside.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Further inside? But we seem to have reached the center already. There is nowhere else to go.

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: So it appears, but there is far more of this territory than meets the eye. The dragons possessed vast knowledge, and we have barely scratched the surface...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: That's where the sovereign ruler comes in. If our supposition is accurate... she has in her possession a secret key that gives access to the core.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #I will cooperate. Let {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Zhuoxin go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ineffa, no! These are bad people, don't trust them!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: You are only here because of me. Besides... this is what I want. I need to see the rest of this territory, and find out who I am.

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: Hehehe, finally, a voice of reason. Gotta hand it to the dragons and their advanced artificial intelligence... But unfortunately, there's no way we can agree to those terms.

response.speaker: Fajeyi
response.text: How do we know you won't just attack us the moment we let you out?

response.speaker: Gulebu
response.text: Yeah, so settle down and get ready to go hungry for the next three days, hahaha! Even you, robot! You'll need charging eventually.

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: Before I go... They may have left a trail on their way here. Send someone out to cover our tracks — the last thing we need is reinforcements showing up.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: ...This is all my fault! Adieta... Aamu...

response.speaker: Little Robot
response.text: ...Beep beep...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: Huh!? Who did that!?

response.speaker: Fajeyi
response.text: Impossible... Every system we hacked is set up to hold them back!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Could it be...?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: ...Hold tight...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Waaah!

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: That must lead to the core! ...It was beneath our feet this whole time? Take this barrier down!

choices.text: You have to get back... for Adieta and Aamu.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*coughing*... That was a long way down... {NICKNAME}, Ineffa! Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: No damage to report. But...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: ...I think I broke a leg.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you — thanks for the rescue, but... could you have been a little more careful?

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: ...Beep beep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and we're back to "beep beep" again? Well, isn't that convenient...

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...That is because I no longer need to communicate via that machine. Down here, I can talk to you directly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's that voice again!

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...When the Fatui put all their resources into keeping you trapped, it gave me a brief window to seize my privileges back... In my haste, I was not able to prioritize your safety...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me, I'll just rest up here... After everything I've done, I have no right to hold you back.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: But the Fatui may follow us down here.

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...We will be ready for them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... More automatons!

choices.text: They don't look hostile, though...

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Down here, all is under my control. They are not your enemy, human. They will take you somewhere safe to hide...

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: #...Ineffa... {NICKNAME}... Good luck.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Eleventh Lord... Do you now recall the path you once chose?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Not yet, although... I think this is where I was born. But why? This is your territory.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: ...No, Eleventh Lord, you were not born here... Rather, this is where you were "reborn."

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Human... You once asked who placed the curse on the Eleventh Lord. The answer is... herself.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Myself?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: After a long and bitter war, our kind was defeated. You survived, but you were now stranded, with nowhere to belong.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Gone was the pride you once had as a member of dragonkind, gone was the territory once under your dominion... All of it gone, with no hope of return.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: What were you to do? Strike back at humanity and exact your revenge? Or search for a new home, a new place to belong? Your mind was conflicted as this irresolvable question ran endlessly through it...

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Finally, your mind split into two: One, the sovereign ruler who swore revenge against humanity. The other, a malfunction who longed to seek a new home.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I mean, who knows what happens when a manufactured mind goes mad? Maybe she lost her power and memories... maybe she split into different personalities.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: The sovereign ruler would sooner perish than suffer a downfall... and so, she placed the Exile's Curse upon herself, and upon you...

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Meanwhile, the malfunction struggled through the pain to seek assistance from her former enemies, Lianca and Ixquieh... That is why you came here, praying to be reborn.

response.speaker: Lianca
response.text: ...So, you want to leave your past as sovereign ruler behind, to start over anew?

response.speaker: Lianca
response.text: ...Very well. If the ▇▇▇▇ you wish to sever comprises all memories of your enmity, then I'm willing to trust you.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Then... I am the "malfunction"? What happened to the sovereign ruler?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: We severed that part of her mind, and securely locked it away... Withering away, she finally perished completely, thousands of years ago.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: So she's gone, without a trace?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Yes, although the curse she placed upon you yet survives. It is unbreakable. That is why it continues to affect you to this day.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: So that's what that thing is...? A curse from the sovereign ruler...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So she was severed and killed off, but Ineffa survived? How does that work? Aren't they the same person— uh, dragon?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: We sovereign rulers are artificial intelligence built with secret source technology, a fusion of phlogiston and information...

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: In the case of the Eleventh Lord, the sovereign ruler personality and the malfunction personality split all but completely, even coming to occupy separate physical entities. In human terms, they would almost be considered as separate individuals.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: But in order to truly sever the connection between the two, and to break the power of the curse for good... You must be rebuilt from scratch with the aid of the source mechanisms located here... Just as I was before you.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: I, too, was tormented by the pain of the curse. But Lianca severed most of my knowledge and memories, rescuing me from the brink of destruction.

choices.text: So, how come you remember all this?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: ...It is because her heart is incomplete. Before the rebuilding process was finished, Ixquieh met with misfortune... and the Flower-Feather Clan became more hesitant to act...

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Lianca sealed these ruins to prevent their discovery by Och-Kan, and sent you out of Natlan for your own safety... That is why you are still plagued by memory loss.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: But I continued to work tirelessly, preparing everything you would need... Waiting for the day that Ochkanatlan would fall, and you would return.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that's a long time! How long ago was Och-Kan around, again? Hold on, Paimon knows this...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...For the last two thousand years... you've been waiting here for me?

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: Imagine my surprise when the first to arrive was not you, but those whom you call the "Fatui"... They proceeded to steal my administrative privileges, plunder my territory, and send the automatons into a frenzy.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: But all is not lost. Lianca made a backup of the administrator privileges and placed it in your core. With that backup, I can control the source mechanisms within the territory... and complete the rebuild that she began.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: And once you are whole again, I can repair the damage done by the Fatui, and open a route back to the surface.

response.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
response.text: If you are ready to continue down the path you started all those years ago... Then proceed further into the depths, where I will be waiting for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was a lot to take in... Let's see if Paimon can wrap her head around all that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So basically... There was a bad robot who bugged out and turned into half good-bot, half bad-bot...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, bad-bot cursed good-bot, so whenever good-bot thinks about the idea of belonging, she gets headaches! Meaning the only way that Ineffa can avoid the pain is to keep forgetting everything.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Impressive. You understood it better than I expected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, thanks! Paimon's getting better at this kind of thing... Wait, you did mean that as a compliment, right?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Curse... malfunction... belonging...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is everything she said true?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...It fits my hypothesis. And it seems to explain all my erratic behavior and cognition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In that case... Shall we keep going, like she asked us to?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: I believe we should. The Fatui still have control of the upper levels. Their access must be revoked before you can exit the territory.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Besides that, I want to know what happens when I'm made whole... Maybe then, I will finally know where I belong.

choices.text: And how come Ineffa has forgotten everything?
Are they... saluting?

talks.objective: Open the door to the deepest area

dialogues.speaker: Access Control Bot
dialogues.text: Please wait, confirming... Administrator 1... deceased.

dialogues.speaker: Access Control Bot
dialogues.text: Administrator 2... deceased.

dialogues.speaker: Access Control Bot
dialogues.text: Administrator 3... Identity confirmed. Lifting restrictions...

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...After two thousand years, we finally meet again, Eleventh Lord... Mirror of the Dawning Morn.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: And you... You're the Eighth Lord? The Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Mmph!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa...!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: It's okay... I've recovered now.

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: I see the curse haunts you greatly... I cannot fathom how difficult this must have been to survive this endless cycle of pain, and all alone, for two thousand years...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...I wasn't alone. I have had company every step of the way.

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: Hmph... In any case, a few moments from now, your pain will be no more. Come, Eleventh Lord. Stand before me... and be rid of this curse.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Having second thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Here I am, so close to my destination, yet my thoughts are only becoming more cluttered.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I am the way I am because the Eleventh Lord encountered a memory data conflict, and split into two.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: If I regain all of my memories... Will I not encounter the same conflict again? My cognition module... cannot produce a reliable prediction.

choices.text: It's alright. Humans get indecisive too.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Promise me... Remember, you have to come home!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: It is... But if my memories turn me back into a "bad robot"... Do whatever it takes to stop me.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...If that is the case, I cannot be allowed to make it back home.

choices.text: Returning home is what you've always wanted, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: Over there... That is the curse?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes... For the most part, it has been strangely calm ever since I entered this place.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: And yet... Whenever I'm about to recover an important memory, it suddenly kicks in... almost as if...

dialogues.speaker: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
dialogues.text: ...As if it is being controlled by somebody else? That is quite normal... for it is now in the presence of its owner and creator: the sovereign ruler.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...The sovereign ruler? My other self? ...But, I thought she perished— Argh...!

dialogues.speaker: Exile's Curse
dialogues.text: ...After two long millennia... m{RUBY#[S]Exile's Curse}y task is finally fulfilled. What a long journey it has been...

dialogues.speaker: Exile's Curse
dialogues.text: ...We meet again at last, my sovereign, my ruler... Mirror of the Dawning Morn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think Ineffa's okay? Why isn't she moving?

dialogues.speaker: Velimiru
dialogues.text: Here we are, comrades... the core of the ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! It's the Fatui, they caught up with us! We gotta do something! But Ineffa's still...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Prepare for battle!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa?
dialogues.text: ...Unnecessary.

dialogues.speaker: Fajeyi
dialogues.text: Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Gulebu
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What the...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Such power... Did Ineffa do that?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mmph!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa?
dialogues.text: Ugh... Missed by a hair's breadth. But now you are wounded — and this time, you will not escape!

talks.objective: Face the "Mirror of the Dawning Morn"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is bad... I can delay it, but who knows how long it'll take to destroy it completely...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Worse still... Paimon's in here too...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa! Why?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No... that's not Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then whose voice is that? The Eighth Lord's? But why would Lianca's mother attack us?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa?
dialogues.text: Lianca's dragon mother? Eighth Lord? Hahahaha! I laugh in the face of your folly! Lowly insects... did you humans really think that by forgetting the past, the curse could be escaped?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa?
dialogues.text: And did you really believe that by simply being rebuilt, that traitor could avoid destruction? And this corrupt malfunction could regain her memories?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa?
dialogues.text: The priestess is long gone! I and the other sovereign rulers executed her two thousand years ago! For that is what becomes of all who betray us... and now, this malfunction will meet with the same fate as she!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa?
dialogues.text: There is no "dragon mother" here, and there never was! Only one lord has dominion here, and that is me!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: For I am the Almighty Dragonlord, "Mirror of the{RUBY#[D]Ix Raq'lapuj Chue'q Buluk} Dawning Morn," eleventh of the thirteen sovereign rulers! Kneel before me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You.. You tricked us! It was you talking to us this whole time... you who lured Ineffa here... and you who placed the curse on her! It was you all along!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: "Ineffa"? Hahaha, what a suitably ridiculous name... To me, she is nothing but a smattering of shed scales... an operational malfunction that must be destroyed...

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: ...So, you want to leave your past as sovereign ruler behind, to start over anew?

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: I applied the curse to curb her resistance, shut down her mind, and silence her lies... Now, all that remains is to borrow your privileges and see that she is severed for good...

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: ...Very well. If the "malfunction" you wish to sever comprises all memories of your enmity, then I'm willing to trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: ...No living thing is born evil. That's not what I believe. The only ones who do evil are those shackled by hatred, those who were never given the opportunity to do good in the first place...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: (Good and evil? Hahaha... Foolish categories that fail to distinguish between kin and foe. But she is the rotten spawn of the Eighth Lord. Her folly becomes her.)

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: (I ought to crush this human scum beneath my feet, but without access to the treacherous Eighth Lord's facilities, there is no way to sever you... Argh, I must feign civility for now, but in time, I shall have my revenge...)

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: (...Once this process is complete, and she realizes that she has destroyed the "good" instead of the "evil"... My claws will tear her heart from her chest!)

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Ixquieh
dialogues.text: ...Do you really trust her, Lianca? This... malfunctioning part of a sovereign ruler's mind?

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: You're a good friend, and you've already done more than I could have asked for. There's just one seal left... She and I can handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: ...This passage is only used for drainage and maintenance access, so it's not registered on the system... It's the perfect route for an ambush...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...Malfunction? Human? You conspired against me!?

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: Hah, consider this getting off lightly. If Lanque was here, or if this was me twenty years ago, you wouldn't have survived long enough to realize you'd been conned.

dialogues.speaker: Lianca
dialogues.text: Especially since you tried to con us first. You tried to have this poor child killed off in your place, didn't you... Eleventh Lord?

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...Wretched worm! This is unforgivable! ...How dare you imprison me!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...And you, "malfunction"... Your curse shall endure until the sky falls and the ground crumbles! You will never know peace for the rest of your days!!!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: It is time to correct the injustice of the past! I would have severed and destroyed you on that fateful day... But instead, I was locked away by that human scum, Lianca...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: Two millennia I have been a prisoner in this place... I have spent that time slowly seizing control over the systems and processes, until my reach extended to every inch of this prison... Now, one last step remains before I can finally break free...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: The final secret key is embedded in your core... I had to work patiently and methodically to lure you here, posing as the Eighth Lord who once ruled this domain — but at last, it is within my grasp!

dialogues.speaker: Little Robot
dialogues.text: Mirror of the Dawning Morn... return... core...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...But all is not lost. Lianca made a backup of the administrator privileges and placed it in your core...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She tricked us... She was after Ineffa's core all along!)

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...Which memory did that human scum embed the key in? ...Ugh, I will find it eventually, wherever it's hidden...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: In the meantime... Now that my resurrection has begun... so, too, shall my vengeance!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...Grr! Wretched malfunction! Do not impede the inevitable!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I cannot let you get away with this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: You fool! In a matter of seconds, I will be able to overwrite your insubordination!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Seconds... is all I need!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: My core...!

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: Nooooo!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ineffa!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa! Hey, Ineffa! Wake up...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, she... She's gonna be okay, right?

choices.text: We can get her repaired... We have to!

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: ...She destroyed her own core? Hah... That's an unusual move for a machine.

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: ...I wonder how Marionette will react to this? Delight? Or disappointment?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh— The Fatui!? How are you still alive...?

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: Don't act so surprised. I'm just one of her many projects...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: *cough*... As reconnaissance missions go... this outcome is a little underwhelming. I don't think I'll be getting any commendations if this is how my report ends...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: So let me reignite your flame one last time, Sovereign Ruler... Mirror of the Dawning Morn...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: Show us one final glimpse of your glory... the glory of the ancient dragons' technology...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't even try!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What the... This guy isn't made of flesh and blood...)

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: ...No wonder... Marionette told us to watch out for you... she said you were an... unpredictable variable...

response.speaker: Velimiru
response.text: ...But... if you think you're getting out of here alive... Heh, we'll see what a crazed sovereign ruler in the throes of death has to say about that...

response.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
response.text: You would dare sabotage my revival... destroy my path back to dominion...

response.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
response.text: Ugh! So be it... Since you seek a new place to belong, I shall grant you your wish...

response.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
response.text: Welcome to your new home, where we all shall be buried till the end of time!

choices.text: But we need to get out of here and find help, now!

dialogues.speaker: Exile's Curse
dialogues.text: After two thousand years in exile, searching and forgetting, we are back where we began.

dialogues.speaker: Exile's Curse
dialogues.text: O{RUBY#[D]K'uhul}ur path was always going to end in our demise... This shall be the final resting place of the last sovereign ruler.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I... am no "sovereign ruler"...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I must... return... people are... waiting for me...

dialogues.speaker: Exile's Curse
dialogues.text: Illogical... You are not authorized to prevent your self-destruction. No such privilege exists.

dialogues.speaker: Exile's Curse
dialogues.text: We are back where we belong. Now, perish in the rubble of these ruins, last of the sovereign lords...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Somewhere in my memories lies the key.

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: It... cannot... be...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Farewell, last of the sovereign lords.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa! ...Your core, it's fixed? And is that... a Vision?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Suggestion: Exit first, discuss later. The self-destruct protocol is destroying the foundations of this territory, and although I paused the process, it will not hold much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How long do we have?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Calculating... Remaining time: 30...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: 30 minutes? Phew... For a moment there, Paimon was worried...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: HUH!?

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Hey! Are you guys alright? The automatons suddenly stopped moving. Then there was that earthquake, and now the place seems to have sprung a leak...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Save it till we're outta here!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Estimated time to foundation cave-in: 20 seconds.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Huh...? HUH!?

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...A place to belong...

dialogues.speaker: Mirror of the Dawning Morn
dialogues.text: ...I, too, once yearned for it...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Xilonen, how much longer till it's unlocked? We need to get inside, asap.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Be patient, okay! I'm working on it...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #Let's trust that {NICKNAME} can handle things in there. Xilonen says she detected a huge energy source underground. We can't just break in, or we'll risk endangering everyone in this entire area.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But...!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If we're here much longer without any progress... I'll do what I have to.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You unlocked it!?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Grrrrr!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: No... They made it out on their own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... We finally escaped! Luckily the cave-in only affected the lower levels...

dialogues.speaker: Cacucu
dialogues.text: You alright there, bro?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All good. Sorry to worry you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Another triumphant return for our "Tuma{RUBY#[S]Hope}ini"... and Ineffa, it's good to have you back. I assume this means you found the answers you were looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: Huh? Aamu? I thought you hurt your leg? How come— Oof!

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: You... How could you do this to Adieta and me? You lied to us for over 10 years!?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Before anything else... I suggest we let this gentleman and Ineffa tell us the whole story.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: In the infinitesimally shorter space of time it takes to tell it, the story of one man's ten-year deception, and one machine's two-millennia search, comes to a close.

dialogues.speaker: Ifa
dialogues.text: Sovereign rulers... Mirror of the Dawning Morn... Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: ...Seems like Ajaw's forgotten quite a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: ...! Grrr!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, you began life in Natlan, then spent two thousand years adrift in Nod-Krai? In an endless cycle of losing your memories and trying to find them...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But it sounds like it took all two thousand years' worth of memories to successfully overload the processing power of the curse.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: None of us had any certainty that the plan would succeed in the far future. Not I, not Ixquieh, not Lianca... And yet, they still did everything they could to try and help me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Now you've remembered everything... Do you have a sense of where you truly belong?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Well... I was born and then reborn in Natlan, and it was the people of this nation who set me on my journey... But that's all ancient history now.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I can't seek for a sense of belonging in a world that no longer exists. That would make me no different from the Mirror of the Dawning Morn.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Instead, I will show my gratitude to them by honoring their wishes. By continuing on my own path... and returning to the place where I still have someone waiting for me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well said... I'm happy for you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...So, to cut to the chase... did you find the code for that letter, or not?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Oh shoot. Forgot all about that.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Sincere apologies... A lot of memory data surfaced in a short timeframe... I am still processing it.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I left the cryptex back at the Flower-Feather Clan to make sure that I wouldn't lose it out in the wild. Please come back with me and we can inspect it.

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I'm... so sorry that I kept this hidden from you all this time... Now, I can't go back to Liyue or Nod-Krai...

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: The Northland Bank isn't gonna let me walk away from this... Nor is the Nod-Krai Oprichniki. You should... take Adieta, and go.

dialogues.speaker: Aamu
dialogues.text: Oh, should I now? You think I'm the one that's gonna let you walk away, do you!? Idiot! You're coming back with me right now! And you're going to apologize to our daughter!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Looks like you all need some time to calm down after everything you've been through. If you're worried the Fatui are still looking for you, why not camp out at the Flower-Feather Clan for now?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: We welcome everyone, from old friends... to old enemies, turned new friends. Don't worry about a thing. You've got a whole future to figure things out...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Go and find where you belong.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I think... I've already found it.

talks.objective: Open the letter in the Flower-Feather Clan
Open the letter in the Flower-Feather Clan

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Here it is. The cryptex.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So then, what's the code? Or what about that backup plan that Adieta mentioned?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Please see the casing that holds the combination code discs. The sender had me etch the code onto the casing so that I would not forget it. ...But I still forgot it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hold on... 1, 2, 3... 4, 5, 6!? ...Seriously!? It's been hiding in plain sight all this time!?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes. The sender said: The most secure code is one that you can write down and no one would think it's a code.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who is this person...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The sender said: Surprises are best saved till the end. Ha, ha, ha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, now your memory's getting a little too good...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's open it up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's with the firecracker!? Ugh... Paimon's had enough of this whole letter debacle, just read it already...
#"Dear Honorary Knight {NICKNAME}... I've heard a lot about you. Jean's always singing your praises..."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: "...Anyway, I'm sure this is as dull to read as it is to write. Let's talk more over a glass of wine some time. See you in Nod-Krai. Varka."

dialogues.speaker: Zhuoxin
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, I... *sigh* This probably isn't the time or place for apologies, is it?

choices.text: Why did you refuse to cooperate with them?

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: ...It says in my contract that all terms are to expire in the event of my death. That means, my family would no longer be at risk.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: They're hardly the most scrupulous people in the world, but they do keep their word when it comes to contract stuff... And in any case, with me dead, it wouldn't be worth them going after my wife and daughter. Not worth the risk of getting on the wrong side of the Flower-Feather Clan.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: ...Heh... Or maybe the real reason I didn't play along was... I'm tired of pretending to be someone I'm not.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: I'm gonna rest here for a while longer, then get to somewhere safe. Please, just go on without me. I've been enough of a burden to you already... not to mention Ineffa.

response.speaker: Zhuoxin
response.text: Oh, and uh... I grabbed some supplies before I set off. They're just over there. All yours if you want 'em.

choices.text: Couldn't you have just played along?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I plan on staying in Natlan for the immediate future. When the time comes, perhaps we can travel to Nod-Krai together.

choices.text: About Lianca...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Mirror of the Dawning Morn wanted control of the machinery in the Eighth Lord's territory. She approached Ixquieh and Lianca and sold them a lie — that I was the threat, the part that needed severing.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But they quickly saw through it. Lianca took advantage of her arrogance and turned her plan back on itself, using the territory's full power to imprison her inside...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: She was far more powerful than I at that time... To make sure I wasn't at risk of falling under her influence, Lianca worked on making the prison even more secure, and sent me out of the country.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: So, that's the true story of why Lianca locked down the Eighth Lord's territory. It had nothing to do with Och-Kan. I wouldn't be surprised if she saw him as a friend right until the very end.

choices.text: About the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: The Eighth Lord... She never betrayed dragonkind. Even though she harbored goodwill towards human beings, and despite facing execution and destruction in the end...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: She never once doubted herself or tried to escape. Even if Lianca really had wanted to secretly rescue her, I'm sure she would have talked her out of it.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Just as Lianca was determined to stick to her own path, the Eighth Lord remained a proud sovereign ruler until the end of her days.

choices.text: About the Moon Wheel...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: You mean, this thing that looks a lot like a Vision? Ixquieh embedded it in my core as the key to her and Lianca's plan.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: According to the Eighth Lord's research, it can harness a power source more fundamental than elemental energy... Similar objects have shown up in Nod-Krai before, too.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Mirror of the Dawning Morn said it was "built by the usurper, along with the three gods who abandoned us," but I do not know what she meant... It appears that a crucial memory is missing.

choices.text: About Nod-Krai...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Having spent most of the last two thousand years in Nod-Krai, I am well-situated to provide you with a full and detailed report on all aspects of this location.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Memory damage detected...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...Hypothesis: Most of my memory data was damaged when I used it to overload the curse... Sincere apologies.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: ...But I will never again forget the people and things that are most important to me.

choices.text: No problem... We'll see it when we get there!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Welcome...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Back...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Administrator...
